questions.question: What is the difference between an aspirational rule and an operational rule?
options: Aspirational rules are paid; operational rules are free
Aspirational rules have no check ('be careful'); operational rules carry a machine-checkable function the workbench can run
Operational rules are longer
Aspirational rules require a manager
questions.explanation: Operational rules are testable; aspirational rules are wishes.

questions.question: What five categories does the lesson cover most rules with?
options: Startup, forbidden, definition of done, uncertainty, approval
Read, write, exec, fork, exit
Plan, act, reflect, refine, ship
Low, medium, high, critical, fatal
questions.explanation: Startup, forbidden, definition of done, uncertainty handling, approval boundaries are the five.

questions.question: What does the lesson say a rule that doesn't fit any of the five categories usually needs?
options: It gets logged as a low-severity warning until someone recategorizes it
It usually wants to be split into two separate, single-purpose rules
It becomes a sixth catch-all category reserved for edge cases
It is dropped from the rule set until a clean category exists
questions.explanation: The lesson says: "A rule that does not fit one of these five usually wants to be two rules. Force the split."

questions.question: What four parts does each rule carry, per the lesson?
options: A slug, a priority score, a named owner, and a scheduled review date
A category, a severity label, an author name, and a changelog entry
A slug, a category, a description, and a named check function
A slug, a long description, a test file path, and a version number
questions.explanation: The lesson says each rule has a slug, a category, a one-line description, and a check field that names a function in rule_checker.py.

questions.question: What happens to stale rules in agent-rules.md, per the lesson?
options: They get moved into a separate archive file for quarterly audit
They get deleted outright rather than left commented out in place
They stay commented out so their history is preserved inline
They get flagged red but stay active until a human approves removal
questions.explanation: The lesson says stale rules get deleted, not commented out, because the workbench is the source of truth, not the chat log of how the team felt last quarter.

questions.question: What does the lesson's reachability test require of the router?
options: Any rule must be reachable within a single hop, inlined in the router
Any rule must be reachable within five hops, described loosely in prose
Any rule must be reachable in two hops, with topic docs linked by path
The whole rule encyclopedia must be re-read fully once per session
questions.explanation: The lesson says the reachability test requires an agent to reach any rule in at most two hops from the router, so the router must link every topic doc by path, not describe it in prose.

questions.question: How do rules relate to framework guardrails?
options: Rules replace guardrails
Guardrails enforce rules at runtime; the rule set is the human-readable contract those guardrails implement
Guardrails are an alternative to rules
Only one of them is required
questions.explanation: Both are needed: runtime catches violations; rule set proves the runtime is doing the right thing.
